What the official sources say

  • Landlord must return the balance of the deposit, without interest, within forty-five (45) days after termination of tenancy, delivery of possession and written demand by the tenant; itemized written statement by mail or in person. (41 O.S. § 115(B); source)
  • If tenant makes no written demand within six months after termination, the deposit reverts to the landlord. (41 O.S. § 115(B); source)
  • On cessation of landlord's interest (including sale), the deposit holder must within a reasonable time transfer deposits to the successor and notify tenants in writing (or return them). (41 O.S. § 115(C); source)
  • Landlord must give at least one (1) day's notice of intent to enter (except emergency/impracticable) and enter only at reasonable times. (41 O.S. § 128; source)
  • Landlord must make all repairs and do whatever is necessary to keep the dwelling unit and premises fit and habitable, and maintain electrical, plumbing, heating and other facilities. (41 O.S. § 118(A); source)

Which law governs renting a house in Oklahoma?

The Oklahoma Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, found at 41 O.S. 101 and following, sets the main rules for residential rentals. It was added in 1978, and section 135 says it is to be liberally construed to carry out its purposes.

Older sections of Title 41, such as the ones on tenancy periods and notices to quit, sit alongside it. A landlord selling a rented house has to read both, because the act covers deposits, repairs, entry and what a sale does to the tenant's rights.

How must an Oklahoma landlord handle a security deposit?

A deposit must be kept in an escrow account at a federally insured institution in Oklahoma. Under 41 O.S. 115(A), misappropriating it is unlawful and can bring up to six months in county jail and a fine of up to twice the amount taken.

When the tenancy ends, the landlord who wants to keep any part must return the balance, without interest, within 45 days after termination, delivery of possession and the tenant's written demand. The landlord has to send an itemized written statement for what was kept.

  • The tenant needs to make a written demand, even if no refund is expected.
  • If no demand is made within six months after the tenancy ends, the deposit reverts to the landlord.
  • Legal Aid Services of Oklahoma adds that a tenant may not treat the deposit as last month's rent unless the landlord agrees.

What repairs does a landlord owe, and what can a tenant do?

Under 41 O.S. 118(A) the landlord must keep the unit fit to live in and keep electrical, plumbing, heating, ventilation and air conditioning supplied by the landlord in working order. Some duties do not apply to single-family homes, such as common-area upkeep, trash containers and supplying water and heat.

Legal Aid explains that for single-family houses the tenant usually pays for utilities and trash service and cares for the lawn unless the lease says otherwise. A landlord and tenant of any home may agree in a conspicuous separate writing that the tenant will do specified repairs or maintenance.

Tenant remedyConditionSource
Repair and deductWritten notice, then 14 days; statute text caps the cost at under $10041 O.S. 121(B)
Repair or move outWritten notice that the tenant will leave 30 days after notice if not fixed in 14 daysLegal Aid
Unlivable homeWritten notice and move out right awayLegal Aid
Essential services cut offWritten notice, then end the rental, fix and deduct, sue for the difference or move and stop paying for that periodLegal Aid

Legal Aid notes the repair-and-deduct limit was set to rise to one month's rent after November 1, 2022, so check the current statute text before relying on the $100 figure.

When can a landlord enter the house?

A landlord must give at least one day's notice before entering, except in an emergency or where notice is impracticable, and entry must be at reasonable times. Section 128 lists the permitted purposes: inspections, necessary or agreed repairs, agreed services, and showing the unit to prospective buyers, lenders, tenants, workers or contractors.

The tenant may not unreasonably refuse. A landlord who is refused may seek an injunction or end the rental agreement. In the other direction, section 124 allows a tenant to seek an injunction or end the rental, and recover actual damages, if the landlord enters unlawfully or harasses with repeated demands.

Legal Aid describes the same rule as 24 hours' notice, which matters to owners lining up photos or buyer visits.

Can a landlord lock out a tenant or cut off services?

No. A landlord who wrongfully removes or excludes a tenant owes damages of up to twice the average monthly rent or twice actual damages, whichever is greater, under 41 O.S. 123. The tenant can recover possession through a court case or end the rental and get deposits and unearned rent back.

Legal Aid adds that a landlord must first send a summons and let the tenant appear in court before moving them out. Owners who want a house vacant for a sale have to use the court process or negotiate a move-out.

What notice ends a tenancy?

The length of a rental decides the notice. If the rental agreement does not fix a definite term in writing, the tenancy is month-to-month, and week-to-week for a roomer or boarder paying weekly.

  • Month-to-month or at-will: 30 days written notice from either side (41 O.S. 111).
  • Shorter than month-to-month: 7 days written notice.
  • Fixed term: ends on its date without notice unless the parties agreed otherwise.
  • Unpaid rent: 5 days after written demand (41 O.S. 131).

A holdover tenant who stays without consent after the term ends can be sued for possession and damages. If the holdover is willful and not in good faith, the landlord may recover up to twice the average monthly rent for each month.

What happens to the lease when the landlord sells?

The lease continues with the new owner. Under 41 O.S. 119, a conveyance by a landlord is valid without the tenant's consent, and rent paid to the seller before written notice of the sale is good against the buyer.

After the tenant gets written notice, rent goes to the successor. The seller is released from obligations for later events, and the successor is liable for all obligations under the rental agreement. Section 114 adds that the successors of landlords and tenants have the same rights, duties and remedies as the people they replace.

A seller should hand the buyer the deposit records too. Oklahoma's flood rule also follows the house: if the premises flooded in the past five years and the landlord knew, section 113a requires that to be stated prominently in writing in any written rental agreement, or the tenant can sue for personal property damage from flooding.

What does a tenant's death or abandonment mean for a rented house?

Two sections cover the awkward cases. When a tenant abandons the unit or is lawfully removed, 41 O.S. 130 lets the landlord dispose of items with no apparent value, and for valuable items requires a certified mail notice, with property left 30 days or more deemed abandoned.

When a sole occupant dies, 41 O.S. 130.1 lets a landlord store the property and hand it to the contact the tenant named, who signs an inventory. The landlord may discard it only after a mailed request goes unanswered for 30 days after the postmark, and must refund the deposit less lawful deductions to the right person.

An heir who inherits a tenant-occupied house inherits these duties, and probate timing can make them harder to meet.

What do Oklahoma landlords who want to sell usually face?

Owners in a state with 77 counties and about 3.96 million people in 2020 face the same statewide act but different local courts. Oklahoma County has 822,125 residents and Tulsa County has 698,782, per Wikipedia's county list, so many rental sales happen in those two courts' areas.

  • Month-to-month tenants who need 30 days of written notice.
  • Deposits that have to be accounted for within 45 days after the tenant's demand.
  • Entry limits when buyers or appraisers want a showing.
  • Tornado Alley weather that damages roofs and triggers repair disputes; the state averages about 62 tornadoes a year.

Selling to a buyer who takes the house with the tenant in place avoids a forced move-out, because the lease carries over under section 119.

More questions about Oklahoma Landlord Tenant Law and Tenant Rights

How long does a landlord have to return a security deposit in Oklahoma?

45 days after the tenancy ends, possession is delivered and the tenant makes a written demand. Under 41 O.S. 115(B), a landlord who keeps part must send an itemized statement, and an unclaimed deposit reverts to the landlord after six months.

How much notice must a landlord give before entering a rented house?

At least one day, except in an emergency or where notice is impracticable. Under 41 O.S. 128 the landlord may enter at reasonable times for inspections, repairs and showing the home to prospective buyers.

Can a tenant withhold rent for repairs in Oklahoma?

Only through the steps the statute allows. A tenant must give written notice, wait 14 days and then may deduct the cost of a qualifying repair, so simply refusing to pay is not safe. Legal Aid also says a tenant who claims the home is unlivable cannot keep living there and refuse rent.

What happens to a tenant's lease if the owner sells the house?

The lease stays in force. The buyer takes over the landlord's obligations under 41 O.S. 119, and the tenant pays rent to the buyer once they have written notice of the sale.

How much notice ends a month-to-month tenancy in Oklahoma?

30 days of written notice from either the landlord or the tenant, under 41 O.S. 111. A tenancy shorter than month-to-month needs 7 days.

Can a landlord change the locks if rent is late?

No. A landlord who excludes a tenant without a court order can owe up to twice the average monthly rent or twice actual damages, whichever is greater, under 41 O.S. 123.

What notices does Oklahoma require before a landlord can file an eviction?

The notice depends on why the landlord wants the tenant out, and the periods range from 5 days to 30 days. The Oklahoma Residential Landlord and Tenant Act at Title 41 sets them, and the court case itself follows Title 12, Sections 1148.1 and following.

A landlord who gets the notice wrong usually has to start over, which costs weeks. That matters to an owner planning to sell, because a rental that cannot be delivered empty or with a clean lease can stall a closing. The table below summarizes the main notices from the statutes we reviewed.

SituationNotice periodStatute
Unpaid rent5 days after written demand41 O.S. 131(B)
Lease violation that can be curedTermination not less than 15 days after receipt, unless fixed within 10 days41 O.S. 132(B)
Repairable damage by the tenant10 days after written notice to fix it41 O.S. 132(A)
Month-to-month tenancyWritten notice at least 30 days before the end date41 O.S. 111(A)
Tenancy shorter than month-to-monthWritten notice at least 7 days before the end date41 O.S. 111(B)
Imminent, irremediable harm or criminal activityNo cure period; eviction may be filed immediately41 O.S. 132(C), (D)

How does the five-day nonpayment notice work?

The landlord makes a written demand for the unpaid rent, and the tenant has five days to pay. If the tenant does not pay in that time, the landlord may end the rental agreement under 41 O.S. Section 131(B).

The statute adds that a demand for past-due rent counts as a demand for possession, so the landlord does not need to send a separate notice to quit. The landlord can send the demand before or after filing a suit for the rent itself, and may sue for the rent at any time after it comes due.

For an owner thinking of selling, the useful point is that nonpayment is the fastest road to possession in the Act. A tenant who pays within the five days stops that particular path.

What happens when the tenant breaks the lease in another way?

The landlord gives a written notice that names the violation, and the lease ends no sooner than 15 days after the tenant receives it, unless the tenant fixes the problem within 10 days. That is 41 O.S. Section 132(B).

  • If the problem can be repaired, replaced or cleaned, the tenant has 10 days after written notice, or less if an emergency requires it.
  • If the tenant does not act, the landlord may enter, do the work and bill the actual and reasonable cost as rent.
  • If the landlord makes the repair, the landlord may not terminate the lease for that violation.
  • A later violation can support immediate termination on written notice.
  • Conduct that threatens imminent and irremediable harm, or criminal activity that endangers others or the property, allows an eviction filing with no cure period.

Section 132 also lists drug-related criminal activity on or near the premises by the tenant, a household member, a guest or someone under the tenant's control as grounds for immediate termination.

How long is notice for a month-to-month tenant?

Either the landlord or the tenant can end a month-to-month or at-will tenancy with written notice served at least 30 days before the termination date. Section 41-111 sets this rule, and it is the usual route when an owner simply wants the house back.

A fixed-term lease ends on its end date with no notice, unless it was ended early under the Act or by agreement. If the tenant stays on without the landlord's consent, the landlord may sue right away for possession and damages. A willful holdover that is not in good faith can add up to twice the average monthly rent, prorated daily. If the landlord agrees to the tenant staying, a month-to-month tenancy is created unless the parties agreed otherwise.

The statute also says how to serve the notice. Personal delivery is the first choice. If the tenant cannot be found, the notice may go to a household member over 12 who lives there, or be posted on the unit with a copy sent by certified mail or through the Firm Mailing Book for Accountable Mail.

What if the occupant has no lease at all?

Section 41-111(G) says the notice rules do not apply to an occupant who has no rental agreement and whose tenancy the landlord never agreed to. The landlord may tell that person to leave without eviction proceedings.

If the person does not leave within a reasonable time, the statute treats it as a trespass punishable by a fine of up to $500. This differs from a tenant who once had permission, so check the facts before choosing which path to follow.

What does the court process look like after the notice period?

The landlord files a forcible entry and detainer action in district court, and the court clerk prepares the affidavit that starts it and the summons. Under 12 O.S. Section 1148.14, an action that fits within small claims limits goes on the small claims docket of the district court.

  • Summons form: it follows a plain-language form developed by the Oklahoma Bar Association, available through the Oklahoma State Courts Network.
  • Hearing date: it must be at least five days after the summons is issued, and the summons must be delivered at least three days before the hearing (12 O.S. 1148.16). Section 1148.5 repeats the three-day rule for service.
  • Title disputes: a defendant who files an affidavit about title or a boundary has 10 days after filing to answer (12 O.S. 1148.6).
  • After judgment: a motion for new trial is due within three days and does not stop execution. The writ tells the sheriff to remove the defendant and give the plaintiff possession (12 O.S. 1148.10).

The statutes we read did not give a dollar figure for the small claims limit, and they did not address appeal deadlines or belongings left behind, so confirm those with the district court clerk.

Why does eviction timing matter when you want to sell a rental?

If the buyer wants the house empty, the notice period and court dates set the earliest realistic closing. A five-day notice followed by a hearing at least five days after summons is the shortest path in the statutes, while a 30-day month-to-month notice before filing adds a month.

The Act also limits what a lease may contain. Under 41 O.S. Section 113, a lease cannot make the tenant give up Act rights, allow a confession of judgment, force the tenant to pay the landlord's attorney fees, or limit the right to call for emergency help. Terms like those are unenforceable, so a landlord should not rely on them to speed things up.

The sources we read do not say what a sale does to an existing tenant's lease. Read the lease and ask an Oklahoma attorney before promising a buyer an empty house. Owners who would rather not wait on a tenant can ask us about an as-is offer for the house.

How do the courts differ across Oklahoma's 77 counties?

Every county has its own district court, so the same statutes are applied in 77 places that range from Oklahoma County at 822,125 residents to Cimarron County at 2,059, per the Wikipedia county list.

The court clerk where the rental sits is the best contact for filing fees, forms and hearing dates. The Oklahoma State Courts Network hosts the summons form named in the statute.

Before sending any notice, keep a simple record: the lease, the rent ledger, the date and method of delivery, and photographs of any damage.

More questions about Oklahoma Eviction Notice Rules

How many days notice does an Oklahoma landlord give for unpaid rent?

Five days after written demand. If the tenant does not pay within five days, the landlord may terminate under 41 O.S. Section 131(B) without a separate notice to quit.

How much notice ends a month-to-month tenancy?

Written notice at least 30 days before the termination date, from either landlord or tenant, under 41 O.S. Section 111(A).

What is the notice for a lease violation?

Written notice that the lease ends not less than 15 days after receipt, unless the tenant fixes the violation within 10 days, under 41 O.S. Section 132(B).

How soon can an eviction hearing be held?

The hearing must be at least five days after the summons is issued, and the summons must be delivered at least three days before the hearing, per 12 O.S. Section 1148.16.

Can a landlord remove a tenant without going to court?

No for a person with a rental agreement, because the sheriff carries out a writ issued by the court after judgment. The statute allows telling an occupant with no agreement and no landlord consent to leave without eviction proceedings.

Can I sell a house that has a tenant in it?

Yes, but the lease and the notice rules still apply. A fixed-term lease ends on its end date, and a month-to-month tenancy needs 30 days written notice from the landlord.
